 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of the petitioner case is as follows:-
That on 26-0-2024 at about 2-45 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in his TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EC-9849 on Kolar - Bangalore NH-75 road and when he reached near Katamanallur fly over, Hosakote, Bangalore Rural dist., at that time the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-HL-0506 came from opposite direction in one way road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Govt., Hospital, Hosakote wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to MVJ hospital, Hosakote, from there he was shifted to East Point hospital, Bengaluru wherein admitted as an inpatient for 7 days.

So far,
the petitioner has spent Rs.70,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, petitioner was a Flower vendor and earning sum of Rs.1,000/- per day.
Due to the permanent disability, he is not in a position to do the said work as earlier.
He has suffered pain, sufferings & loss of income.
4. In response to the issuance of summons/notice the respondent No.2 did not appear before this tribunal and has remained absent.
Hence he was placed Ex-parte.

5. The respondent No.1/the Insurer of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-HL-0506 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.1 has contended that even though the break system of the vehicle of the petitioner was in order, the petitioner having no driving licence and having no competency to ride the TVS XL rode the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the insured motorcycle and that as per the medical records petitioner inter alia suffered traumatic head injury which clearly demonstrates the fact that by not wearing headgear he was riding the motorcycle hence the accident in question has occurred due to the sole negligence on the Nagaraj K vs Magma Hdi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38189959/
2 part of the petitioner.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 26.10.2024 at about 2.45 p.m., near Katama Nallur fly over, on Kolar - Bangalore NH- 75 road, Hosakote, Bangalore Rural Dist., due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-HL-0506?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?

sentences.text: If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What order or Award ?
7. The petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 got examined its Assistant Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and 2.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.1 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 53/HL-0506, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 26-0- 2024 at about 2-45 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in his TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EC- 9849 on Kolar - Bangalore NH-75 road and when he reached near Katamanallur fly over, Hosakote, Bangalore Rural dist., at that time the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-HL-0506 (herein after called as the offending vehicle) came from opposite direction in one way road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle,
result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as FIR with Complaint, Spot mahazar, Seizure mahazar, Notice U/sec.133 of MV Act, reply to the notice, IMV report, Wound certificate & Charge sheet, etc.,

3 12.

sentences.text: On the basis of the complaint lodged by the son of petitioner i.e., Sri.Adikeshava .N. case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle by Hosakote Traffic Police in Crime No.316/2024, for the offences punishable under section 125(b) and 281 BNS.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under section 125(b) and 281 BNS.
13.
The respondent no.1 neither in their written statement nor during the cross examination of PW.1 has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

The respondent no.1 has taken the contention that though the petitioner has contended that at the time of accident the insured vehicle was proceeding on the wrong side of the road but except placing reliance on the charge sheet, the petitioner has failed to substantiate the said contention with any other material.

It is further argued that in the absence of spot sketch to determine the direction of insured vehicle and the vehicle being driven by the petitioner on the road, there is no reason to believe that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and that the petitioner in connivance with the investigating authorities has filed false case against the driver of the offending vehicle.

14. If the documents placed on record is perused, it is true that the petitioner has not produced the spot sketch but the petitioner has relied upon the spot mahazar to prove that at the time of accident,
offending vehicle was proceeding from opposite direction in one way road against to the traffic rules.
If spot mahazar is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 32 feet.
The petitioner was proceeding from Hosakote towards K R Puram ie., Kolar - Bengaluru road.
The spot of accident is on the left side of the said road.

When the said road is a double road and it is one way road, when offending vehicle was proceeding from opposite direction ie., from Bengaluru - Kolar road he ought not to have drive his vehicle on the one way road opposite to the road from which the petitioner was proceeding.
Hence, entering the vehicle in one way road in opposite direction itself tantamount to negligence contributed by the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is nowhere stated by the respondent no.1 the road in which the offending vehicle was proceeding if not it was proceeding on the opposite direction in Kolar- Bangalore road.
The respondent no.1 has not taken any steps to examine the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the investigating officer after thorough investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

When there is no rebuttal evidence from the side of respondent no.1 regarding this issue as they have not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the eye witness to the accident, this court has to rely upon the police documents and oral evidence of petitioner and on such reliance this court is of the opinion that petitioner has proved issue no.1.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., wound certificate and discharge summary which are at Ex.P6 and Ex.P8.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at East Point Hospital, Bengaluru from 26-10-2024 to 31.10.2024 for a period of 5 days.
As per the wound certificate, petitioner has sustained four injuries of which injury no.1 & 2 are simple in nature and injury no.3 and 4 are grievous in nature.

sentences.text: The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to him and there is no evidence on record to say that petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
As such there is no loss of future income.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
17. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained grievous and simple injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc., it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
18. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced medical bills for sum of Rs.28,273/- at Ex.P10.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.28,273/- under the head medical expenses.
19. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 49 years.
He was flower vendor by profession and earning Rs.1,000/- per day.
In order to prove the same, petitioner has not produced any document.

Hence considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and place of residence this court has taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
20.
As per the discharge summary, petitioner has taken treatment for 5 days as an inpatient at East Point Hospital, Bengaluru.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for two months.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.33,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.

21. Further for 5 days of hospitalization as an inpatient at East Point Hospital, Bengaluru and for his taking follow up treatment, requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment, for follow-ups, has incurred traveling expenses, he has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/-.
22 . The petitioner at his age of 49 years has suffered injuries, which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.1,50,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.75,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs.28,273/-
 3. Towards loss of income Rs.33,000/-
 during laid up period  4. Towards Conveyance, Rs.25,000/-
 Attendant charges and  nourishing food Nagaraj K vs Magma Hdi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38189959/
5  5. Loss of discomfort and Rs.1,50,000/-
 amenities

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,11,273/- (Rupees Three Lakh Eleven Thousand Two Hundred Seventy Three only).
23.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 1 st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
24. Issue No.3:- In the light of the findings given on Issue No. 1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,11,273/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Eleven Thousand Two Hundred Seventy Three only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit entire compensation amount is ordered to be released in favour of the petitioner on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 5th day of March 2026.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
